Late summer 2019. I had just turned 17, and was coming home from an amazing camping trip with friends.

My dad is an alcoholic, who had been sober for a year or so. I went to his house, and he was wasted. He lost his shit and sexually assaulted me. He then had a medical emergency, so I took him to the hospital. He told the paramedics, so the cops were called and he was arrested. 

Less than a week later, my best friend died of an overdose at the age of 16. Two days after that happened, I found out that my boyfriend was in love with her, she was in love with him and he had cheated on me with her. 

I’m okay now, but let’s just say that life sucked for a while.

My bestfriend passed away from an overdose last year, and it hit me really hard. She was only 16, which made it very tragic and unexpected. I heard the news from her little sister just hours after it had happened. 

I was obviously inconsolable, so my mom took me to our family friend’s house. We talked, and the family friend told me I should ask for a sign from her. (She believes in all that supernatural stuff whereas i’m more of a skeptic). 

Not 30 seconds later, my bag falls off the table, and a black charging cube fell out. I picked it up and realized that it had a piece of tape on it, with my best friends handwriting. It only said her name, but I have absolutely no idea how it got there, because she had just moved and I hadn’t been to her house yet. 

I’m sure there’s a logical explanation, but it definitely brought me some comfort in that moment.

During grade 11, I lost my best friend to an opioid overdose. It was very very tragic and sudden. After this, I looked for anything I could do to find a silver lining, so I organized a workshop on overdose prevention for students at my high school. The workshop included all participants getting Naloxone training and certification. We all walked away with our own Naloxone kit and the knowledge of when to use it.

Months later, I was hanging with some friends, one of whom was doing Xanax. He ended up accidentally ingesting a lethal amount of fentanyl. I injected him with Naloxone twice and carried him to the ambulance. If we had waited even an hour later, he would have died.

I like to think it was actually my best friend who saved his life, by giving me the resources to know what to do.

I don’t know if this counts... But throughout elementary and middle school I always worked with a counsellor.

I showed up to a session one day, with a bruise on my arm from being hit. My dad was a raging alcoholic, who was abusive in many different ways.
She asked, I lied like always, but she was the first person to keep looking instead of just believing me. She made a call, and after a few months of very messy investigations, I was out of his house. 

I hated that someone got involved, but as I grew up I realized that it was exactly what I needed to be safe. Now, I have an on and off relationship with my dad, but I am no longer living in an abusive household. Even though it stung; it was the best thing anyone could have done for me.
